concept: Stat is one named figure read the way a device prints a reading: the name on the body's inset line, the number and its unit alone in a recessed window, and an optional change printed under the window as a glyph, a word and an amount. It says one thing and is never pressed.

default_to_avoid.pattern: stat card: a floating tile with a big bold number and a green up arrow or red down arrow for the change
default_to_avoid.why_not: The tile floats on the page with its own shadow, and the green and red tell the change by colour alone, but P2 asks for a window cut into the body and P5 allows no tinted text.

default_to_avoid.pattern: stat figure that counts up from zero when it appears
default_to_avoid.why_not: A count-up is entry choreography and shows wrong numbers on the way, while P2 and P6 want the value to change at once.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the figure sits alone in a recessed window with its name printed on the case
Braun LE 1 speaker (Dieter Rams, 1959): a printed legend beside the part, never inside it
system/FORM.md display class: window recessed into the body, value with the unit beside it

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The figure sits alone in a window that takes surface.sunken, elevation.well and a hairline ring, so it reads as a reading cut into the plastic and never as a tile.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The name is printed above the window on the same inset line as the window's edge, and the change is printed under it on that line too.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: The figure and the change amount use tabular numerals, so a new reading keeps its width; the unit is a smaller medium weight beside the number.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes
derivation.form: Every word is primary or secondary ink and the change is told by a glyph and a word, never by a green or a red.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: A Stat is a reading and never a control, so nothing in it is orange, however good or bad the change.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: An empty reading prints a dash in the same window, so a missing value does not change the height of the Stat.

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: The root is a labelled group with nothing focusable; set live and it becomes a polite status that reads the whole reading.

options.name: printed name, figure alone in a recessed window, change printed under
everything printed on the body, a large figure over a hairline rule
one dark window holding the name, the figure and the change

variants.reason: A keeps the window for the reading alone and prints the name and the change on the body, so a row of Stats reads as several windows and not as a dashboard; B has no window and drifts to the large bold number of a KPI tile, and C copies the OLED Display and moves the name into the light.

root.why: A grid of three rows, the name, the window and the change, all on one inset line, with a gap that does not change when a row is absent.

label.why: The name is printed above the window in caption size on the inset line and names the group for assistive tech.

window.why: A recess with inverse light and a hairline ring holds the figure alone, so the reading is the only thing cut into the body.

figure.why: The number is set in medium weight with tabular numerals, start-aligned in the window, and steps with the size.

unit.why: The unit sits beside the number at label size in secondary ink, so the number stays the loudest ink in the window.

reading.why: When there is no value the window prints a dash and this hidden text says No reading for assistive tech.

change.why: One printed line under the window, on the inset line, holds the glyph, the word, the amount and the comparison.

word.why: The direction is written as a word in medium weight beside its glyph, so change is never told by colour.

amount.why: The size of the change keeps tabular numerals so it lines up from one Stat to the next in a row.

compare.why: What the change is measured against, such as since yesterday, is printed in secondary ink at caption size.

sm.why: Small Stats set the figure at emphasis size for dense rows beside other readings.

md.why: The default sets the figure at title size, big enough to read at a glance and smaller than a Display.

lg.why: Large Stats set the figure at display size for the one number a whole sheet is about.

data-empty.why: With no value the figure prints a dash in secondary ink inside the same window, so the Stat keeps its height.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window keeps a real border drawn in the text colour so the recess still reads.
